q: My birth plan is to labor at home for as long as possible, and transition to the hospital around 4-1-1. My parents will be around at our house with us during labor. We've had a prenatal doula and birthing classes, but will not have a doula present at labor or birth.
c: First-time mum, six minutes from the hospital, thinking of having both parents and her husband in the room.

q: Just curious if anyone has ever had their dad in the room during labor and delivery? I know it would mean so much to him, but he by no means expects it or has even brought it up.
c: Same author.

q: My first two pregnancies were an absolute breeze, mild morning sickness, I would throw up and go about my day, no round ligament pain, no lightning crotch, no pregnancy exhaustion, just uncomfortable sleep positions. This one though? All of it, and more.
c: Third pregnancy in four years, due in July, two toddlers at home.

q: To anyone out there who has/had easy pregnancies and is thinking they'll all be that way, I truly hope they are I wouldnt wish this on my worst enemy.
c: Same author.

q: Also lightning crotch is so awful, I had read about it with my first pregnancies but I dont think it was described well enough bc why do I feel like I'm splitting it two sometimes.
c: Same author.

q: My mil tells me I'm glowing and my mood swings make we want to scream about it.
c: Same author; says her in-laws are kind.

q: The last time I made a comment about back pain on tiktok under another mothers post about pregnancy struggles my inbox was flooded with people telling me Im not allowed to complain about something I chose to do. :'(
c: Same author, surprised Reddit replies were kind.

q: Right now everyone said that since this pregnancy is so much harder it must be a girl lol.
c: Same author, two boys so far.

q: We came in for reassurance about the fall and left with more questions than answers.
c: 22+5 weeks with her second; two scans 11 days apart gave very different measurements. Crossposted to r/BabyBumps.

q: I’m just not finding any information on these symptoms and whether they’re normal or not. I messaged the obgyn practice and waiting to hear back.
c: First-time mum at 13 weeks, sick since 5 weeks, on new anti-nausea medication.

q: after this visit, the next time his friend is planning to stay down will be the week when my baby is due to arrive. I already know I won’t even be allowed to have that personal bonding time with my first baby and it’s upsetting me already.
c: 4 months into her first pregnancy (UK); partner's friend stays for days at a time, stepdaughters stay most weekends.

q: My partner also mentioned to his daughter that during the summer holidays, she can come and stay for the whole time (which I believe is about 6-8weeks) and I’m already feeling the pressure of this, as this will then leave me with only around 6 weeks before I am due to give birth.
c: Same author.

q: For 3 of my appointments I've just had an email that my appointment has changed days before the appointment itself. I usually book them in for the morning so my husband can come with me and the midwife often changes to the middle of the day and a different day.
c: UK; her work is flexible, her husband's isn't.

q: I told her I can't make the new appointment and asked for it to be moved back within minutes of the reschedule but she said no and that the next appointment she has is another week away.
c: Same author.

q: By 10:30pm, no one had been to see us - no exam, discussion or obs, let alone being started off. The bay lights were turned off so we were left sat in the dark just waiting and getting more and more anxious about what was happening.
c: UK; called in for an induction she was never keen on, placed in a caesarean recovery bay; they self-discharged.

q: I had a really bad experience with a consultant who insisted I had to be induced with no discussion, then following the dopplers was told there was no need for concern as long as blood flow, fluid and movements remained okay.
c: Same author, induction offered for slightly tailing growth.

q: wrong information, wrong due date etc - so my trust level is already pretty low.
c: Same author on errors in her notes at every appointment.

q: I am 30 weeks pregnant with my 1st so navigating what is “normal” or “expected” has been tricky sometimes🤣
c: UK, asking others about symptoms before her midwife appointment.

q: I wish I could just eat like the pregnant ladies in the movies 😭.
c: Almost 34 weeks (UK), on a strict diet for a pregnancy condition, hungry between hourly snacks.

q: The reason I am hurt is that I feel like a burden to him (at one point he said that he was running around me like a fool) and I know it will get worse once the baby comes, as I will need more support in the first few weeks.
c: First-time mum at 35+5, resting before a planned caesarean; husband plans a night away at his country house.

q: I hate being weak and depending on someone, but I don't know how to avoid that in this stage.
c: Same author; they later agreed he would go for two days.

q: I brought it up to him and he got upset and said that it was my personality and that I’m just too much of a downer for him to be turned on by me.
c: Five months into her first pregnancy; on intimacy with her husband. Crossposted to r/BabyBumps.

q: At this point I wish he would just say the generic thing all men say about “it’s weird that there’s a baby in there” but he doesn’t, he basically makes it my fault.
c: Same author.
